title: Zach Bryan Wears ‘Free Palestine’ Shirt at Robert Kraft’s Gillette Stadium
summary: It comes after Macklemore was dropped from the remaining U.S. dates of Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour over the rapper’s pro-Palestinian statements.
contentText:
Grammy winner Zach Bryan took a pointed fashion stance at Gillette Stadium on Friday night (Oct. 2), wearing a black T-shirt reading “Free Palestine” during the first of two dates on his With Heaven On Tour at the Foxborough, Mass., venue.

Members of Bryan’s band were also spotted in matching shirts, according to TMZ , with fan footage of the moment quickly circulating on social media. Bryan did not appear to address the shirt from the stage.

The choice of wardrobe — and venue — is hard to read as a coincidence. Gillette Stadium is owned by the Kraft Group, led by New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, who weeks earlier played a central role in removing Macklemore from the remaining U.S. dates of Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour over the rapper’s pro-Palestinian statements onstage.

During his opening sets at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J., on Sept. 4 and 5, Macklemore declared “Free Palestine” to the crowd and performed his 2024 protest song “Hind’s Hall.” On the second night, he also spoke directly to Jewish fans in attendance, saying his criticism of the Israeli government was not directed at them.

The Israeli-American Council launched a petition calling for his removal, and on Sept. 14 tour promoter Messina Touring Group confirmed Macklemore would no longer appear on the remaining U.S. dates after multiple NFL stadium owners reportedly threatened to pull shows if he stayed on the bill.

Kraft confirmed his involvement in a statement that same day, saying he felt a responsibility to speak up when he believed a line had been crossed on antisemitism, while acknowledging that Palestinian suffering is real.

Sheeran said in his own statement the following day that the removal was the promoter’s decision, not his, and that he had spoken directly with Kraft while trying to find a resolution.

The fallout was swift. Fellow openers Finneas, Aaron Rowe and Lukas Graham exited the tour in solidarity, as did Irish folk band Beoga, who had been performing with Sheeran, while Macklemore responded with a lengthy Instagram post detailing the money, brand deals, festivals and private shows he says his advocacy has cost him.

He later pledged $1 million from his touring earnings to Palestinian aid organizations and announced a Free Palestine Tour — a short European run hitting Dublin, Paris and London from Oct. 26 to 30 — which he has since said sold out immediately.

Sheeran never made it to Foxborough in the end: his two Gillette Stadium dates last weekend were scrapped due to severe weather conditions — despite the tour having bowed to the venue owners’ demands.

Bryan has rarely shied away from friction with powerful figures. In October 2025, a teaser of his song “Bad News” — which references ICE raids — drew public criticism from the Department of Homeland Security and the White House, with Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem saying at the time that she was disappointed by the clip. Bryan pushed back at the time, arguing that the song spoke to both sides of the aisle and urging fans not to let social media narratives divide them. The track ultimately appeared on his album With Heaven on Top , released Jan. 9, 2026.

Bryan is scheduled to return to Gillette Stadium for the second night of his Foxborough stand on Saturday (Oct. 3) — and all eyes will be on whether the shirt makes a repeat appearance, and whether Kraft, who has yet to publicly respond, takes any action. Representatives for Kraft did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
